targets.authors: Lupyan, G., Rakison, D. H., & McClelland, J. L.
targets.title: Language is not Just for Talking: Redundant Labels Facilitate Learning of Novel Categories.
targets.evidence_quote:
We replicated Experiment 2 from Lupyan et al. (2007), specifically the finding that
participants learn object categories faster when they are given labels compared to
when they have no labels, or other nonlinguistic cues.
targets.outcome_quote:
Even though the replication data show a partial replication of the primary analysis of
interest (the main effect of Condition), the lack of a Condition x Block interaction fails
to support the main claim made in the original paper: adults learn categories quicker
if they have labels versus when they do not. Additionally, the fact that the Auditory
Label and No Label groups did not have a significant difference in performance, while
the Written Label group performed significantly lower than the Auditory Label group
but not different than the Location group, suggests that having a label is not always
beneficial in this category learning task.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly select mixed in section 4.3 Brief Evaluation, an overall verdict. Section 4 explains the partial replication of the main effect and absence of the interaction. This overall evaluation governs despite the abstract saying the key result failed. The conceptual pilot also failed and adds no independent original target.

reasoning: Full manuscript title and three authors match the assignment. Experiment 2 of the single Lupyan et al. paper is directly retested with new participants. Other cited label studies are background or original-author commentary, not targets.
